summary: Fixed the revision-1 relay-merge-gate design defect: the status only re-evaluated on pull_request events, so a Director MERGE_APPROVED commit (a push to main, not a PR event) could never turn it green, deadlocking a legitimate approved merge if made required. Added a gate-refresh job to .github/workflows/relay-merge-gate.yml that runs on push to main touching .ai-ops/state.json and republishes the same relay-merge-gate commit-status context for every open [RELAY ...] PR against the freshly pushed state, via a new pure planRefreshStatuses function and its I/O wrapper scripts/publish-relay-merge-gate-status.mjs. The original PR-triggered job, the shared evaluateMergeGate invariant, and relay-automerge.yml/relay-fastlane.yml are unchanged. Documented that the exact required-check identity is the Statuses API context string 'relay-merge-gate' (exported as MERGE_GATE_STATUS_CONTEXT), not a GitHub Actions check-run name.
root_cause_evidence: Revision 1's root-cause finding is preserved and unchanged: PP-RELAY-057 PR #104 and PP-RELAY-058 PRs #105/#106 merged to main while state.json still recorded a pre-approval status; merged_by on all three is the repository owner's own account, not relay-automerge.yml's automation, and none carry relay-automerge.yml's forced '[RELAY <task>] Director-approved squash merge' commit title. relay-automerge.yml and relay-fastlane.yml were re-confirmed as already correctly gated on MERGE_APPROVED with exact PR/head matching; .ai-ops/fastlane.json remains disabled with an empty allowlist. The gap is that GitHub permits any account with merge rights to squash-merge an open, green, non-draft PR directly regardless of state.json; only a required-status-check (or equivalent) branch protection rule can prevent that. Director review of revision 1 (PR #107, closed unmerged) additionally found that its pull_request-only trigger would never re-run once state.json changed via a push to main after the PR was already open, which this revision fixes.
design_correction: Added a second job (gate-refresh) triggered by push to main on the .ai-ops/state.json path, which lists currently open PRs targeting main, filters to [RELAY <task-id>]-titled ones, and republishes a relay-merge-gate status for each head using the same evaluateMergeGate invariant (via the new planRefreshStatuses pure function). Neither job mutates any PR head; both only publish a commit status against the exact SHA under evaluation, so an approval never authorizes a head other than the one it was recorded for, and a later push to the same PR branch flips it back to blocking.

Also enable 'Do not allow bypassing the above settings' (including for administrators) on that same rule, since the account that performed the PP-RELAY-057/-058 out-of-band merges has merge rights on main and would otherwise still be able to bypass a required check. No tool available to this Relay worker can read or modify branch protection/ruleset settings. See .ai-ops/README.md's Mechanical auto-merge contract for the full explanation.
